verdicts.evidence: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139; base version wrapped with updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}
verdicts.reason: The old Update computed the object once, then passed &updateWrapper{updated: obj} to Legacy.Update so both stores wrote identical content; the new code hands the raw objInfo to both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update. pkg/registry/apis/playlist/legacy_storage.go:141 calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) again against the *legacy* old object, so the two stores can end up with different content.

Inside the DeleteCollection goroutine the duration of d.Legacy.DeleteCollection is fed to d.recordStorageDuration, which writes to DualWriterStorageDuration (metrics.go:59); every other legacy call in the file uses recordLegacyDuration.

Delete builds `log` with name/kind/method on line 96 but then does klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) on line 97, so downstream code reading the logger from ctx loses those values. Every other method in the file passes `log`.

All four goroutines do context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) on the incoming request context. net/http cancels the request context as soon as ServeHTTP returns (and the apiserver's timeout filter cancels earlier), and the handler returns immediately after `go func()`, so the legacy write runs on an already-cancelled context; pkg/registry/apis/playlist/legacy_storage.go passes that ctx straight to the SQL service.

Each goroutine assigns the legacy error to a variable used only as the is_error metric label — no log.Error call anywhere, unlike the synchronous paths. There is also no defer/recover, so a panic in a legacy store implementation takes down the whole process instead of failing one request.

Same finding as c002: the DeleteCollection goroutine records the legacy call with recordStorageDuration. The cited line number is off (166 in the file, 165-166 of the added hunk) but the identifier and function are exactly right.

All four sub-points check out: `var method = "create"` etc. should be const; line 59 returns `err` which is provably nil after the line-43 guard; `const mode3Str` sits between Mode() and Create() whereas mode2Str is at the top of dualwriter_mode2.go:25; and the Create comment still says it writes to LegacyStorage first while dualwriter.go:59-61's DualWriter doc claims a legacy-first, skip-storage-on-error contract that mode 3 no longer follows.

Same defect as c004 stated more narrowly: the background contexts are children of the request ctx, so request completion cancels them. The 10-second timeout can only shorten, never extend, the parent's lifetime.

legacyStoreMock and storageMock embed the *same* *mock.Mock instance (created as `m := &mock.Mock{}` and shared), so the `m.On("Create", mock.Anything, failingObj, ...)` expectation matches the Storage.Create call too. storageMock.Create sees name=="object-fail" and returns args.Error(1); nothing panics and the storage error path is exercised. The test is confusingly written but the stated consequence is false.

objInfo is passed to Storage.Update and then, unchanged, to Legacy.Update in the goroutine. legacyStorage.Update calls objInfo.UpdatedObject a second time against the legacy `old` object, so patch/apply transformations are re-applied from a different base — exactly what the removed updateWrapper existed to prevent.

The goroutine passes the request object `obj` to Legacy.Create while `created` (with the fields unified storage assigned) is what gets returned to the client. Mode 2 deliberately runs enrichLegacyObject to reconcile the two before the second write; mode 3 has no equivalent, so anything the unified store assigns is not reflected in the legacy row.

Mode 3 hands the caller's obj/options pointers to the goroutine with no copy, whereas mode 1 in the same package deep-copies before spawning — so the concern is not idle. But the object the handler serializes is `created`, a different pointer, and I cannot check whether k8s.io/apiserver's handlers touch obj/options after the storage call returns: there is no module cache and no network in this environment. Reading k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/create.go, or a `go test -race` run, would settle it.

SetDualWritingMode defaults currentMode to Mode1 when the KV store has no entry, and the only transitions it implements are 1<->2; desiredMode==Mode3 falls straight through and returns Mode1. So the three new DualWriterDesiredModes: Mode3 subtests construct a DualWriterMode1, and the new mode-3 production code is never entered by them (the etcd one is t.Skip'd on top of that).

verdicts.evidence: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101-105; removed apierrors.IsNotFound branch in the diff
verdicts.reason: The base version explicitly swallowed apierrors.IsNotFound from Storage.Delete and still called Legacy.Delete; the new code returns on any error before reaching the goroutine, and the apierrors import was dropped. An object present only in legacy can now never be cleaned up.

Three different conventions in one package: a package-level `var p = prometheus.NewRegistry()` in mode1_test, a local `p := ...` in dualwriter_test, and — added by this change — a local `p :=` in exactly one of the six new TestMode3_* functions that shadows the package-level p, while the other five use it.

verdicts.evidence: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:522-531 (GET /api/playlists right after client.Resource.Create) and getFromBothAPIs calls
verdicts.reason: doPlaylistTests asserts the legacy /api/playlists response matches the UIDs immediately after the k8s creates, and checks both APIs after each update — under mode 3 those legacy writes are fire-and-forget goroutines with no synchronisation, so the assertions race. Latent today only because of c013 (the subtests actually run mode 1); it becomes a flake the moment mode 3 selection works.

legacyStoreMock and storageMock both embed the same *mock.Mock, so an `On("Create", ...)` expectation cannot distinguish which backend was called — which is precisely what mode 3 tests need to assert. It is also what makes the TestMode3_Create failure case pass by accident (see c009).

Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection each repeat the same go func / WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New(...)) / defer cancel / record-duration block with only the store call differing. The copy-paste is also how the c002 and c025 mistakes got in.

verdicts.evidence: go.work.sum:404 and go.work.sum:408 (identical lines); diff.patch lines 14-19,37-54,72
verdicts.reason: The change adds a byte-identical duplicate of the github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery .../go.mod line (grep shows it at both 404 and 408), plus grafana-azure-sdk-go, prometheus-alertmanager, otel and genproto entries that have nothing to do with the dual writer.

Correct on both the mechanism and the fix: all four goroutines derive from the request ctx, which the HTTP server cancels once the handler returns, so the 10s timeout never gets to matter; a detached base (context.Background/WithoutCancel carrying the request values) is what is needed.

In Create and Update, the failure branch of the *storage* call records d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...). The success branches two lines below correctly use recordStorageDuration, so error latencies land in the wrong histogram and the storage is_error="true" series is always empty.

options.Kind is the TypeMeta of the *options* struct (metav1.CreateOptions/UpdateOptions/DeleteOptions, metainternalversion.ListOptions), not of the resource. The apiserver builds those from query parameters via the parameter codec, which never populates TypeMeta, so the kind label collapses to "" for real traffic — only the unit tests set it, by hand-constructing options with TypeMeta{Kind: "foo"}. I could not open k8s.io/apiserver to quote the decode path (no module cache), hence the reduced confidence, but the label is the options object's kind either way.

Same defect as c004/c020. "Systematically only completes half" overstates it — whether the legacy call gets far enough before cancellation is a race, not a certainty — but the underlying claim about reusing the request context and losing legacy writes is correct.
Same defect as c004, stated conditionally. The apiserver does cancel the request context on completion, so the conditional resolves true.

The success branch of Delete passes `name` where every other recorder call in the file passes options.Kind, including the error branch three lines above and the legacy recorder in the goroutine. Beyond the inconsistency this puts a per-object identifier into a Prometheus label, so the histogram's cardinality grows with the number of deleted objects.
Same finding as c002/c006, stated plainly: the legacy DeleteCollection duration goes to recordStorageDuration.

verdicts.evidence: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection assert only on the returned object
verdicts.reason: None of the new tests assert that Legacy.* was called, and none wait for the goroutine, so the async legacy write — the entire behavioural change in this PR — is untested. With the shared mock (c017) such an assertion could not be written as the tests currently stand.
